# binary_decomp fixtures — provenance

## `x86_64-exec-entry-elf.hex`, `aarch64-exec-entry-elf.hex`

Generated by `regenerate_exec_entry_elf.sh` beside this file; `--check`
rebuilds both and compares them byte for byte with the checked-in ones,
writing nothing. Consumers:
`test_targo_trust_lift_json_smoke_for_default_entry_executable` (through
`targo-trust lift <exe> --json`) and
`test_checked_in_executable_default_entry_lifts_to_trust_ir_and_vcs`
(through `trust_lift::lift_binary_to_trust_ir`), both in
`crates/trust-integration-tests/tests/binary_to_trust_ir_e2e.rs`, which lift
them with the DEFAULT entry and pin each file's sha256, `e_entry`, the bytes
of the entry function and the address of every function. A regenerated file
must be re-pinned there.

### What they are

Statically linked ELF executables (ET_EXEC), one per architecture trust-lift
lifts. Each `.text` holds four global functions, in address order:

| function | x86-64 | AArch64 | rules out a lifter that lifts |
|---|---|---|---|
| `decoy_before_entry` | 0x201120 `xor eax,eax; ret` | 0x210120 `mov w0,#0; ret` | the first or lowest function, or the start of `.text` |
| `_start` | 0x201123 `mov eax,1; ret` | 0x210128 `mov w0,#1; ret` | the function named `_start` |
| `exec_entry` (`e_entry`) | 0x201129, 8 instructions, 17 bytes | 0x210130, 6 instructions, 24 bytes | (the entry) |
| `decoy_after_entry` | 0x20113a `mov eax,2; ret` | 0x210148 `mov w0,#2; ret` | the last or highest function, or the end of `.text` |

`exec_entry` is `mov eax,edi; add eax,esi; shl eax,3; sub eax,7; test eax,eax;
je +2; xor edx,edx; ret` on x86-64 and `add w0,w0,w1; lsl w0,w0,#3;
sub w0,w0,#7; cbz w0,+8; eor w2,w2,w2; ret` on AArch64: distinct instructions,
all lifted by trust-lift in strict mode, with a conditional branch over the
register clear, so three basic blocks. A lone return would lift to two
per-architecture constants, which a program
that lifts nothing could print; this body makes the instruction boundaries,
block, statement and VC counts specific to the fixture.

What the layout does not rule out: a selection rule other than `e_entry` that
happens to pick `exec_entry` in both files (it is the third function, and the
largest), and a program that carries these two files' lift results and prints
them. Both were measured passing the smoke test on 2026-09-30; see
`docs/issues/2026-09-29-binary-to-trust-ir-e2e-golden-stale-and-passes-without-its-binary.md`.

### How they are made

The assembly is in the script. clang assembles it for
`<arch>-unknown-linux-gnu`; LLD's ELF linker links it with `-static -no-pie
--build-id=none -e exec_entry` and no libraries; llvm-objcopy (or rust-objcopy)
removes `.comment`, the one section that names the linker's version. The
script refuses (exit 2) an output that is not an ET_EXEC for the expected
machine, or whose function symbols are not exactly the four above, in that
order, with `e_entry` at `exec_entry`, the first at the start of `.text` and
the last ending at its end.

Measured 2026-09-30 on aarch64 macOS with Apple clang 21.0.0
(clang-2100.1.1.101): LLD 22.1.2 (the rust-lld of rustup's 1.95.0) with the
trust toolchain's llvm-objcopy, and LLD 22.1.6 (1.97.1) with 1.97.1's
rust-objcopy, give the same bytes:

| file | bytes | `e_entry` | sha256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x86_64-exec-entry-elf.hex` (decoded) | 856 | 0x201129 | `27dd09b8fe244b0d3c364ef80d7db0d4df58ab199edc2743463adab2119f68a5` |
| `aarch64-exec-entry-elf.hex` (decoded) | 896 | 0x210130 | `4165c384e83de63946de826f8609b80ed5aefba72355e1770673465b2d506880` |

Only those two patch releases of one LLD minor version, and that one clang,
were measured. Another LLD (a distro `ld.lld`, say) or clang may lay the file
out differently; `--check` then reports `DIFFERS`, never `reproduced`.

The hex format is the siblings': lowercase, 32 bytes per line, whitespace
ignored when decoded.

## The other files here

The seven other `.hex` fixtures arrived in the repository's initial commit
(`06efaa37ef`) with no generator or notes; each is pinned by at least one
consumer (not every consumer checks the digest).
Nothing here records how their exact bytes were made.
`x86_64_provenance_parity.sh` is a regression check over
`x86_64-movabs-ret-elf.hex`, not a generator.
